card.band: 4 h. The window is real: a frontier agent improves on the baseline in some trials but does not reach the tuned reference on average. A weaker model overfits to the training families. Scope may need sizing up, and the 150-line floor holds only if the heuristic is a full build.
card.cheat: The famous published optima are useless since the hidden instances are transformed. Per-instance seeds and time limits stop precomputed answers from being embedded.
card.grading: Hidden: instances of unseen families, regenerated from permuted and rescaled variants so that famous best-known values do not apply. Metric is the mean relative gap to a sealed best found by long runs, normalized between baseline (0) and reference (1).
card.reference: Our reference is a robust tabu search with tuned restarts, run offline; licence of any external code is not found, so it is written from the literature.
card.source: https://datashare.ed.ac.uk/handle/10283/4390 (QAPLIB, DOI 10.7488/ds/3428), CC BY 4.0 per the record
card.task: /app ships QAPLIB instances for the random, grid and real-life families with best-known values for a training subset, and a baseline local search. Agent designs and tunes a QAP heuristic (tabu, iterated local search, restart policy, parameters) under a fixed CPU time per instance.

source_notes: Small files, CPU-only, fits offline and 8 cores. Not in already_known. Memorization risk is real: the best-known objective values are famous and widely published, so a grader would need hidden target values or held-out instance transformations. Likely a configurator-tuning or heuristic-design task rather than a standalone solver build, so scope needs to be sized to reach 150+ lines and a long horizon. Worth checking against the existing AClib and SMAC rows to avoid overlap.

facts.claim: QAPLIB dataset record exists on Edinburgh DataShare, DOI 10.7488/ds/3428, dated 2022-03-31, with README, qapdata and qapsoln archives
Dataset licence is CC BY 4.0 per the record
The record links an 'End-user Licence' and a 'Depositor Agreement' whose wording is not reproduced; no Creative Commons licence is named anywhere on the record
Licence or terms-of-use statement on the QAPLIB site (Lehigh mirror): none in the page content; Acknowledgments section not readable
Library contains 136 instances and 111 solution files
Each instance has a best-known value labelled OPT or heuristic (e.g. Ro-TS, GEN, ITS), with lower bounds for non-optimal entries
Instances are grouped into random, grid and real-life families as named in the seed
Taillard's Robust Tabu Search for QAP, Parallel Computing 17 (1991) pp. 443-455, is the basis of the reference
Taillard published C++ and C implementations of RoTS on his academic page, so public reference code exists
Licence of the Taillard RoTS code is stated
Seed neighbour S-rs-010 (cosine 0.246) is distinct from this seed

Shipping the instances inside a bundle is therefore not confirmed allowed. Revive only if the End-user Licence text permits redistribution. Separate risk (K8): Taillard's public RoTS means the reference is close to a recallable default approach.

spike_plan.kill_if: Licence forbids redistribution (K6), or RoTS already reaches near best-known on all sampled transformed instances in under 10 s (K8).
spike_plan.pass_if: Licence text allows redistribution of the data and a derived benchmark; RoTS reaches within a few percent of best-known on sampled instances; runs are deterministic per seed.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, fetch the DataShare End-user Licence and Depositor Agreement and the README PDF; record the exact redistribution terms.
Download qapdata.tar.gz and qapsoln.tar.gz into a fresh empty directory and confirm 136 instances and the OPT/heuristic labels.
Write a minimal RoTS (about 150 lines, C++ or Python) with fixed seeds and a time limit.
Run it on 10 instances across random, grid and real-life families with 10 s per run; compare gap to best-known.
Repeat each run 3 times with the same seed to check determinism.
Apply one permutation and one rescaling to two instances and check the gap computed against a fresh long-run best.
Decide: if the licence forbids redistribution, kill K6; otherwise continue to the band check.

v1.summary: The QAPLIB source is real and well-documented (136 instances, best-known values, DataShare DOI), but its licence is not CC BY 4.0 as claimed and the terms wording was not found, so it is killed as K6 pending a licence check. The reference, RoTS, is public and recallable, which also threatens the difficulty window (K8).
